clue.text: Silver went after gold here

parts.note: Silver is not the metal but Long John Silver, the pirate of Stevenson's novel, who hunted buried gold on a remote isle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' and 'gold' look like a pair of metals or medals, but Silver is the one-legged pirate of R. L. Stevenson's adventure story, and the answer is its title and setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel is set on the isle where the pirate Long John Silver seeks Captain Flint's buried hoard.

clue.text: Visible -.remains of an ancient undertaking

parts.note: an undertaking here is the undertaker's trade, a burial, and the visible remains are the earth mounds raised over ancient graves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaking' reads as an enterprise or project, but it means a burial, the undertaker's job; ancient burial mounds still stand in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrows heaped over prehistoric graves are still visible features of the landscape, the lasting trace of old burials.

clue.text: Record-making start to the student year?

definitions.text: Record-making start to the student year?

parts.words: Record-making start to the student year?
parts.note: record-making suggests breaking a record, but it means putting names on a register, which is how a student's year begins

explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-making' hints at a record-breaking feat; here it is the literal making of a record, signing students onto the register.
explanation.definitionFit: Registration of new students on the college roll happens at the start of the academic year and creates the official list.

clue.text: Grounds for development?

parts.note: grounds suggests reasons or justification, but here it is literal plots of land set aside for building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds for' reads as 'reasons for'; it is plots of land where builders develop.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots of land earmarked for building projects are places where construction is planned.

clue.text: Charging for a sign on pottery

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another is written above it

parts.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a potter's stamp on a pot might cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' looks like asking a price for a mark on a pot; it means rushing headlong at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull charging at a gate is butting into it head first, driving hard against it.

clue.text: See 1
Coach has to remain outside as required by law

indicators.note: the word for remaining is placed around the other piece, sitting outside it

parts.note: to stay is to remain
a coach who teaches privately is a tutor

explanation.surface: A trainer must legally wait outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a bus or a sports trainer; here it is a private teacher, and 'outside' wraps the remaining word round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid down by Act of Parliament is legally mandatory, prescribed by a statute.

clue.text: Bill free of bitterness?

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to be rid of something is to be free of it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man called Bill has shed all his resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or taste that stings is sharp and harsh, full of bitterness.

clue.text: The sort of contest that goes on in the ring

definitions.text: The sort of contest that goes on in the ring

parts.words: The sort of contest that goes on in the ring
parts.note: the ring is a boxing ring where a hard, evenly matched fight goes on, and also the ringing of a bell

explanation.walkthrough: The ring is both the boxing ring and the sound a bell makes; a fierce, see-saw contest is named after a bell's peal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-fought, evenly matched fight swinging back and forth is likened to the to-and-fro clang of a bell.

clue.text: Note when the army order is given

parts.note: to mark something is to note it
a time is a when, the moment something happens

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to write down the moment a command is issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a musical note or a written memo; it is the verb, to mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling soldiers to march on the spot without advancing.

clue.text: Two chaps, one customer

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men walk into a shop but only one buys anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular shopper who supports a business is its client.

clue.text: Seen in church when spring'

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Seen in church when spring'' ends on a stray apostrophe and is cut short: 'when spring' gives AS + SPA, which cannot make the whole answer without a missing indicator or word

clue.text: Calms and sends to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Lulls are quiet spells, pauses in a storm or activity; as a verb it means soothing someone into slumber.

clue.text: .I'm beaten and confined

parts.note: I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe
pounded means beaten repeatedly

explanation.surface: A prisoner complains of being beaten and locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray animal or seized car is shut away in a pound, held in custody.

clue.text: Girl on the cricket-side is not a true member

parts.note: Peg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A woman fielding on one side of a cricket pitch is not really in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member; it is a limb, and a wooden leg is no real limb. In cricket the leg side is the half of the field nearest the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden replacement for an amputated leg is an artificial limb, not a natural one.

clue.text: With us details can produce weariness

indicators.note: producing something new from these letters means rearranging them into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Joining in with the fine print would wear anyone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can produce' rearranges the letters of US DETAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental fatigue and lack of energy.

clue.text: Possibly one ain't from a good school

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in some other order

parts.note: ain't gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone using the word 'ain't' is surely not from a posh school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the letters of ONE and AINT. ETON is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated at Eton College, Britain's best-known fee-paying school, comes from a prestigious establishment.

clue.text: Neither here nor, there

parts.note: the comma splits the idiom so it reads as something that is at neither place, being between the two

explanation.walkthrough: The stray comma turns the idiom 'neither here nor there' (irrelevant) into a literal description of goods or people travelling between two points.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or travellers on their way are between departure point and destination, at neither end.

clue.text: One slum I refurbish — with this?

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes something, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A council plans to do up a run-down tenement and asks what to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbish' rearranges the letters of ONE, SLUM and I. The definition reads off the surface: you might do up a slum using this kind of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is the water-based paint used to decorate walls when doing up a room.

clue.text: Miss tea when involved in painting

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An artist skips the tea break when absorbed in work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of MISS TEA. 'Painting' looks like the activity; it is a canvas, a work by the French painter Henri Matisse.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas by Henri Matisse, the French Fauvist artist, is called by his name.

clue.text: They may be consumed from cups

definitions.text: They may be consumed from cups

parts.words: They may be consumed from cups
parts.note: cups suggests drinks, but these are eaten boiled, sitting in small holders at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed from cups' suggests tea or coffee; the cups here are breakfast egg cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-boiled at breakfast, they are served upright in small holders and eaten with a spoon.

clue.text: Beast retiring with toe broken too

parts.note: a retiring person is shy, coy

indicators.note: a broken foot part has its letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal limps off having hurt its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges TOE to OTE. 'Retiring' suggests leaving or going to bed; it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie wolf of North America is a wild animal, a beast.

clue.text: Upset? Depends bow bigheaded one is!

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bigheaded' usually means conceited; here it means having a literally large head, which decides what hat fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a boat is to tip it over; read as two words, it is the measurement of a hat, which varies with head size.

clue.text: Guard is fed up to death

indicators.note: in a down clue the word fed is read from the bottom up

parts.note: death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A sentry announces he is sick and tired of the whole business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up to death' reads as an idiom for being utterly bored; 'up' reverses FED to DEF, and death gives END.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect someone from attack is to shield them, keep them safe.

clue.text: Improving — using a reference book?

explanation.definitionFit: Things getting better are on the up; and a reader checks a word in a dictionary by searching it there.

clue.text: Love to have a role in pictures

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Someone wants to land a part in films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' suggests films, matching 'a role'; it is a 1960s style of painting built on optical illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1960s abstract style of art using geometric patterns to create optical effects, so a type of picture.

clue.text: Love to have a tea break about five. Like an egg?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed around the Roman numeral, surrounding it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

indicators.note: break signals that the letters of the drink are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone sweet on a cuppa takes a tea break at about five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges TEA to ATE; O and ATE then go 'about' V, giving O-V-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate describes an oval shape, broader at one end, as an egg is.

clue.text: Eccentric when out and about

parts.note: out is taken as written
re is Latin for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone acts oddly whenever they are out and about town.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré describes something unconventional, beyond the bounds of the normal.

clue.text: take road transport to America, he tried flying

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'take road transport to America, he tried flying' opens in lower case with a word lost: the wordplay I + CAR + US needs a leading 'I' that the held clue does not print, and no scan is available
annotationWithheld.clue: take road transport to America, he tried flying

clue.text: Aversion is stated another way -

indicators.note: putting something another way means rewording it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's dislike is being expressed in different words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another way' rearranges the letters of IS STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or repugnance.

clue.text: In June the rates will be lower

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A householder learns that local taxes will fall in early summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like a verb about cutting rates; it is an adjective meaning further down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or underneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Didn't stay uninhabited

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who ran off abandoned his post; an abandoned, empty town has nobody living there.
